## Budgets and the budget series (`BudgetConsumer`, `BudgetSeries`) {#sec-ch10-budget}

### Summary

A budget output, `- {type: budget, dt: ...}`, reads the register after every accepted step and writes one record per
interval to a NetCDF time series. A record holds, per conserved row, the domain total, its change over the interval
and the transfer out through the domain's boundary faces, plus the monitor's counters and minima. Without sources,
the change and the boundary transfer cancel. At the pin the budget reads the step fields and the counts; it does not
yet read the amounts of @sec-ch10-amounts.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Per interval and row: total, change, boundary transfer, @eq-ch10-budget; summed counters and minimum minima.

**Data.** In: the conserved state, the step fields $S_d$, the face areas, the solid mask, the monitor. Out: a `BudgetRecord` per interval; `<basename>.budget.nc`.

**Placement.** `observe` after an accepted step, in `MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo`; `flush` at the output's cadence and on the final write.

**Activation.** An output of type `budget`; it requests a step field in every active direction.

**Guarantee / limits.** FP64 sums; closes on the boundary transfer to $10^{-12}$ relative in the test deck; no source, fixer or residual columns yet.

**Evidence.** `test_budget.<b>`, `test_conservation_budget.<b>` (Tests).
:::

Local symbols: $Q_r$ is the interior total of row $r$, $\Delta Q_r$ its change over an interval, $B_r$ the summed
outward transfer of row $r$ through the counted faces over the interval's steps, $\sigma_f \in \{-1,0,1\}$ the
outward sign of face $f$.

### Derivation

The finite-volume update changes a cell total only by the fluxes through its faces and by sources. Summed over the
interior, the interior faces cancel in pairs and only the boundary faces remain. Each accepted step's transfer
through a face is its step field times its area (@eq-ch10-stepfield), so over an interval

$$
\Delta Q_r + B_r = \text{sources}_r, \qquad B_r = \sum_{\text{steps}} \sum_{d} \sum_{f} \sigma_f\,A_f\,S_{d,r,f},
$$ {#eq-ch10-budget}

where the inner sum runs over the faces the consumer counts. With no source, fixer or floor active,
$\Delta Q_r + B_r = 0$ up to round-off. The right-hand side is what the amounts would supply; at the pin the
consumer has no column for it.

### Numerical method

**The output.** `BudgetOutput::bind` requests the step field of every active direction of the hydro register
({{< code src/output/budget_series.cpp BudgetOutput::bind >}}). After an accepted step `apply_redo` calls
`observe` on every output ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}), which passes the
register and its monitor to the consumer ({{< code src/output/budget_series.cpp BudgetOutput::observe >}}).

**Observe.** The first observe starts the interval after its own step, so that step stays out
({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp BudgetConsumer::observe >}}). Every later observe adds the step's boundary
transfer, adds the monitor's counters and takes the minimum of its minima.

**The counted faces.** `boundary` builds, once, an outward weight per face, the sign times the face area, over the
faces of the interior cells ({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp BudgetConsumer::boundary >}}). A block face counts
when a boundary function acts on it and it is not periodic: the wall, outflow and custom faces, not interior, seam
or periodic faces ({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp boundary_face >}}). With a solid, every face with exactly one
solid neighbour counts, outward from the fluid cell, and a block face whose interior cell is solid does not. The
transfer is the sum of the weighted step field per row, in FP64.

**Flush and series.** `flush` closes the interval: the new totals, their change, the summed transfer, counters and
minima, the time, interval and cycle ({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp BudgetConsumer::flush >}}). The totals are
the interior sums of the state times the cell volume ({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp BudgetConsumer::totals >}}).
`write_output_file` waits for the last local block, sums the blocks in order and then over the processes
({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp reduce_budget >}}), and the root process appends the record
({{< code src/output/budget_series.cpp BudgetOutput::write_output_file >}}). The series file holds time, cycle, dt,
interval, the row, counter and minimum names, and total, change, boundary, counter and minimum, sums as `NC_DOUBLE`
and counts as `NC_INT64` ({{< code src/output/budget_series.hpp BudgetSeries >}}). A restart saves the open
interval's sums as a carry and resumes them ({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp BudgetConsumer::carry >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_budget.<b>` (`every_row_closes_on_the_boundary_transfer`) | on a two-block dry slab with an outflow $x_1$ and no source, every row of every record after the first satisfies @eq-ch10-budget with zero sources, and mass leaves | $\lvert\Delta Q_r + B_r\rvert < 10^{-12}\max(\lvert Q_r\rvert, \lvert B_r\rvert)$ | set inline ({{< code tests/test_budget.cpp Budget.every_row_closes_on_the_boundary_transfer >}}) |
| `test_budget.<b>` (`a_restart_resumes_the_interval_from_its_carry`) | every record after a restart inside an interval equals the uninterrupted run's | exact (`torch::equal` on every field) | ({{< code tests/test_budget.cpp Budget.a_restart_resumes_the_interval_from_its_carry >}}) |
| `test_budget.<b>` (`a_file_without_a_carry_starts_at_the_first_observe`) | a deck without a budget output writes no carry; resumed with one, its first record has an empty interval and no change, and the next record's interval is the sum of its steps and closes | exact on the empty record and the interval; $10^{-12}$ relative on the closure, as row 1 | ({{< code tests/test_budget.cpp Budget.a_file_without_a_carry_starts_at_the_first_observe >}}) |
| `test_conservation_budget.<b>`, `test_conservation_budget_mp.<b>` | on 15 closed decks (walls, periodic $x_2$, moist, cubed sphere, rain), the domain totals of mass, energy plus potential energy, species and, where periodic, $x_2$ momentum or the axial angular momentum drift less than $4n\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ after $n$ steps; the $x_1$ walls pass no mass | $C\,n\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$, $C = 4$ | set at the top of the test ({{< code tests/test_conservation_budget.cpp Budget.closes_to_round_off >}}) |

: Tests of the budget. {#tbl-ch10-budget-tests}

All pass at the pin, on CPU (@tbl-ch10-ctest-run). `test_conservation_budget` checks the conservation the budget
reports on closed decks; it does not read a `BudgetRecord`.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The budget has no source, fixer or residual columns at the pin: they are a later step of the output lane
  (`O8-cols`; {{< code src/diagnostics/budget.hpp BudgetConsumer >}}). A run with an active source, fixer or floor
  shows a nonzero $\Delta Q_r + B_r$ that the record does not attribute.
- With the face-flux covariance on, its default, the energy row misses about $3\times10^{-11}$ of its total per
  interval, because the covariance energy increment is not in the register's boundary-face fluxes. The test deck turns
  the covariance off for that reason; the size is the comment at the head of `tests/test_budget.yaml`, not a
  measurement of this chapter.
:::

1. **The `_cuda` entries were not run.** `test_budget_cuda` and `test_conservation_budget_cuda` exist for CUDA
   builds; this chapter's run had none.
